frames.slice_level: Upper thorax, at or just above the aortic arch (approximately T2-T4). Trachea round and midline; no arch contour resolved.
Carina / proximal main bronchi, approximately T5-T6. Airway seen centrally as a transverse lucency at the bifurcation.
Below the carina, at the main bronchi / bronchus intermedius, approximately T6-T7. Both bronchi visible as paired lucencies within the mediastinum.
Lower thorax at heart level, approximately T7-T8. Heart occupies most of the mediastinum; bronchus intermedius and left lower lobe bronchus visible as paired lucencies.

cases.impression: Four contiguous axial levels of an unenhanced chest CT — upper thorax, carina, main bronchi, and heart level — on soft-tissue window. The upper three levels are unremarkable, as previously recorded. On the lowest frame the lower lobes come substantially into view for the first time, and the posteromedial right lower lobe shows a cluster of small rounded and short branching opacities that is more crowded than the corresponding left-sided region. The leading explanation is crowded normal lower-lobe vasculature, which is exactly what this window and this level produce; the asymmetry is the only feature arguing otherwise, and it is not enough on its own. This cannot be resolved on a soft-tissue window — distinguishing vessels from small nodules or tree-in-bud needs a lung window through the same level. Elsewhere the lungs are well aerated and extend to the chest wall, with no consolidation, mass, or pneumothorax. Subtle dependent grey posteriorly in both lungs is within the range of normal supine dependent change and is not recorded as a finding. Airway patent and midline throughout. The heart occupies most of the mediastinum at the lowest level with no discrete mass; chamber size and pericardium are not assessable on an unenhanced single axial frame. Bones intact throughout, with no fracture or lytic or sclerotic lesion.
